summary: The waterfront park that the Port's June 2026 report lists among Mission Rock's completed Phase 1 elements as the '5-acre China Basin Park' (other Port documents give its size as 4.4 acres in 2018 and 'almost five acres' in 2025); SF YIMBY reports that SCAPE Studio was responsible for its master design and that Webcor was the general contractor. An opening celebration was held on the morning before SF YIMBY's April 26, 2024 article. The Port says the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure, including parks.

milestones.text: Opening celebration held for China Basin Park (SF YIMBY's April 26, 2024 article says it was held 'yesterday morning', so April 25)

Port Commission passes Resolutions 25-05 and 25-06 unanimously to accept Phase 1 public infrastructure; staff say 'First is China Basin Park and Port open spaces' and that the park will be 'completely Port owned'
Port staff report says the Developer completed Phase 1 in 2025 and 'the City has accepted all public infrastructure, including parks, streets, and public utilities within the Phase'

open_questions: No cost for the park as a whole is published in any source read. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo (Table 1, Expected Final Budget) has a Phase 1 hard-cost line labelled 'Inland CBP' of $27,397,300 (2019 approved budget), $33,395,979 (2021 approved budget) and $39,184,050 to $40,657,253 (revised low and high estimates). These are budget figures, not final costs, and the table shows no separate line for shoreline or in-water work.
The Port's 5-acre figure and the mapped lot area differ; which boundary the Port counts is not stated.

The Port's October 2023 memo says the 2021 Phase 1 budget increases did not include 'in-water' work 'being delayed to a later phase', and describes 'a revised schedule for the construction of China Basin Park inland and shoreline components'. No source read says whether any park shoreline or in-water work remains outstanding.

Area of China Basin Park: the Port's June 2026 staff report says 'the 5-acre China Basin Park'; earlier Port documents say '4.4 acre China Basin Park' (January 26, 2018 staff report) and 'almost five acres' (staff remarks, February 11, 2025 minutes). Pier & Point's mapped lot 8719A005 is about 4.69 acres less the Block K lobe, so the figures are not directly comparable.
